say: Grim's in the dirt and the whole yard has gone quiet.
Somebody put down the biggest dog in the swamp. Now we find out who holds the leash.
She grew this business from a handful of seeds and a foul temper. Who waters it now?
I owed Grim my life twice. Third time I'm paying it back in blood, whoever it takes.
Hash sits in the sheds. Buyers sit in the bar. Nobody sits in her chair.
They'll say the Hounds are finished. Let them say it. From a long way off.
The one who did it walks around like it's nothing. We know the face. That was clever of nobody.
A pack without a head bites its own. Watch your back at the sheds tonight.
Blackshifters are already measuring Shark for new curtains. Over my corpse.
She'd have laughed. She'd have called it sloppy work and then she'd have hunted the killer down personal.
Debt doesn't die with the lender. Whoever took her owes us all, and we keep ledgers.
I keep reaching for the hemp price list and she's not there to shout at me about it.
Grim's dead. Shark just got a lot more interesting, and a lot more dangerous.
The Hounds without Grim are a rabid animal with no master. Stay out of their alleys.
Every gang in the swamp is counting its knives tonight. Somebody will take her docks.
Crazy Grim, they called her. Clever, too. Clever and crazy is a hard thing to bury.
Hemp doesn't care who owns the field. It just wants a hand to pull it.
I drank to her when I heard. Not because I liked her. Because it could've been any of us.
The Hounds are open for the taking. Don't make that face.
Our boss has been waiting years for Shark to open up like this. Tonight he's smiling.
Grim sent a nice letter once. Spelled like a drunk. Pity it ends like this.
Take the docks first. Then the sheds. Then whatever's left breathing in her HQ.
Whoever finishes her pack gets the swamp's money. Whoever hesitates gets buried by the winner.
Hash is going to cost double this season. Some swamp queen got herself killed.
The Hounds' boss is dead. Someone strolled into Shark and ended her. Just like that, people say.
Her gang grew half the hemp on the continent. Now who do the smugglers answer to?
I heard a thousand Hounds died with her. I also heard it was one person. Pick the story you like.
My supplier went quiet. Said something about a dead boss and a lot of shouting.
Swamp business again. Somebody big got killed. I'm told it's good for the price of everything.
Big Grim fell, so I hear. A warrior who falls in the open has had a better end than most flatskins earn.
Word came over the border. Big Grim is dead. We nodded, and went back to our cups. The hemp trade will feel it.
I didn't know Big Grim. I know the sort. The sort ends the way it ended.
A flatskin name has gone quiet. I heard it from a trader. I did not ask for the rest. The swamp will sort out its own.
No tears from me for Big Grim. Okran's mercy has limits, and the road marks them.
Big Grim is dead. The Flame doesn't weep for sinners. It does keep count. The hemp trade will feel it.
People say Big Grim is dead. Okran sees all, and has now seen the end of that one.
Big Grim has been struck down. Pray the deed was clean, and pray it was not ours to answer for. The swamp will sort out its own.
They've got Grim in a cage. A cage! Somebody tell me which one of us is going to open it.
She's alive, and that's worse, because now we have to do something about it.
Grim doesn't beg. If she's quiet, she's counting the bars and counting the ones who put her there.
Pack's frantic. No leader at the docks, no word in the sheds.
Whoever holds her wants something, or he'd have killed her. Find out what and pay it.
Big Grim, locked up. Someone's playing for the whole swamp, and it isn't any of us.
I'd pay good cats to see her face behind bars. Then I'd run before she got out.
The Hounds are howling. A caged boss is a loud thing.
A live Grim is worth more than a dead one to somebody. Ask who gains. Then ask who's fastest with a key.
Shark's got a vacancy and a jailer, and both are going to get someone killed.
Some swamp gangster got locked away. The hemp dealers are in a panic over it.
Big boss from the swamp is in chains, people say. Never thought I'd hear that one.
Smugglers say their queen has been taken alive. I say that's an invitation for a rescue and a bloodbath.
Did you hear? Somebody caught the Hounds' boss. Alive. The swamp is not happy about it.
Big Grim held in chains. Honour is for the fallen. A caged man has none to spend.
They keep Big Grim alive. I wonder what it gets them. In the Kingdom we call that a mistake. The swamp will want her back.
Big Grim is taken alive. A cage is a poor end for anyone with a blade. The flatskins call it mercy.
They took Big Grim and did not kill them. In the Kingdom we would ask what the blade was for. Hemp prices will tell the story.
They hold Big Grim in chains. A cell is the first step toward confession.
Big Grim, caged. Pray they are asked the right questions. The swamp will want her back.
Big Grim lives on in a cage. Okran gives even the lost a chance to repent, though few use it.
Chains for Big Grim. If the chains are honest, the Flame is satisfied. Hemp prices will tell the story.
Big Grim runs the swamp's green, and she's crazy enough to like it that way.
Mind your tongue about Grim. She may not read well. She remembers everything you say.
Plant the hemp, drop the hash, bring home the cats. That's Grim's whole sermon.
Nobody crosses the Hounds who wants to see Shark in the morning.
They say Grim is touched. I say touched is what you call it when you can't match her.
That's the one. That's the one who took Grim.
You've got her blood on you and it hasn't dried.
No cage, no mercy. You took our head, now we take yours.
Grim gave this swamp its food and you gave it a hole. Come here and pay for it.
You've got Grim shut up somewhere. Open the door or we open you.
Where's she? Tell me where she's and I might let you die quick.
The leash is off. Every Hound in the swamp is looking for your face now.
You took the boss alive. Stupid or brave? Doesn't matter, you'll find out which.
You're the one who killed Grim. Keep walking and don't touch a thing in here.
Heard you ended the Hounds' boss. Heard it was a quiet job.
Everyone wants to shake your hand and no one wants to be seen doing it.
That's the one who got Grim. I'm not looking. I'm very much not looking.
I hear you're connected to the Hounds' trouble. Do me a favour and pretend we never met.
Swamp folk say a stranger killed their queen. Strangers like you, perhaps?
You've got a look. The look of someone who made a hash dealer's week very bad.
The swamp's queen is dead and I hear a stranger did it. Don't look so pleased, friend.
If you're the Grim killer, keep that quiet around anyone selling hash.
Thanks for Grim. We owe you one, and we pay what we owe. Mostly.
Don't expect a parade. Just know that the right people in Shark are very glad.
You did the swamp a favour that nobody will admit to. Here, have a drink.
Best thing that happened to Shark in years. Stay our friend and you'll see it pay.
Darkbrow gone? Then you've been busy in my swamp. Mind where you step next.
That crooked fool had it coming. Don't take my thanks for a welcome.
You did him, did you? Ha. Now my left side is clear and my right side is nervous.
One less snake in Shark. Don't mistake me for grateful. Don't mistake me for stupid.
Gray's finished. Honest man, honest fool. Hard to say which killed him.
Those Grayflayers will go to the Swampers now. I don't like the smell of that.
Gray didn't deserve that. I'll tell you so, then I'll tell you to leave.
You cut the Grayflayers down to nothing. The swamp will charge you for it.
Big Al, dead? Good. My people will be at the Stone Rat Village before the sun's up.
Al's gone. His rats can scurry to me or run to the ninjas. Tell them to choose quick.
Big Al's dead? Then the rat-hole is mine. Don't expect a thank you note, my letters are poor.
Good. One lunatic fewer. I'm saving the rest for myself.
Al's dead. Who the hell do we answer to now? Anyone? Hello?
He was a lunatic and he was ours. I'm going to miss that screaming.
The village is jumpy. Hounds on one side, ninjas on the other, and us with no boss.
We shook down outposts for him. Who's going to tell us who to shake down next?
First rat to run is the first rat the ninjas eat. Stay put. Stay quiet.
I told Al the day would come. I just never thought I'd be standing here for it.
The Rat Village will fall to the Hounds or the ninjas by the end of the week. Mark it.
Stone Rats have nothing to charge anyone for now. No more raids. No more protection.
Al held that village with spit and nerve. Take away the nerve and see what stays up.
Outposts all over the swamp will sleep easier. Too bad about the ones who'll sleep forever.
Hounds want the village for the hemp. Ninjas want it for the pride. Rats want it for nothing now.
Big Al, the mad one, finally got cut down. Whoever did it did the road a favour.
The Stone Rats won't be asking for protection money anymore.
A rat is a rat. When the head goes, the nest goes with it. That's what they say, anyway.
Something happened in the swamp and half the scavengers I know are cheering.
Al raised hell on outposts for years. Somebody finally sent it back to him.
Big Al is dead and the Stone Golem did not stir. It does not stir for such as that.
So Big Al is gone. Let the flatskins fight over what's left. They always do. The outposts will sleep better.
Big Al fell, I heard. A warrior who falls in the open has had a better end than most flatskins earn.
Word came over the border. Big Al is dead. We nodded, and went back to our cups. The Stone Rats will fight over the scraps.
So Big Al is dead. Another sin put out. The Flame burns clean, and the ash is sensible about it.
Big Al is gone. Say a prayer for the soul, if it had one. Then keep walking. The outposts will sleep better.
No tears from me for Big Al. Okran's mercy has limits, and the road marks them.
Big Al is dead. The Flame doesn't weep for sinners. It does keep count. The Stone Rats will fight over the scraps.
Al's in chains. Can you believe it? Al! I'd heard it takes a dozen men.
They took the boss alive. That's worse than dead.
If he's not back by dawn, I'm taking my knife and walking to the Hounds.
Somebody will free him. Somebody always frees a madman. That's how they stay mad.
Big Al's under lock and key. First time that man has been quiet in his life.
Stone Rats leaderless again. Raids will either stop or double.
Someone dragged Al off alive. Wouldn't have the nerve myself.
Big Al in chains. Somebody's got nerve.
Stone Rats leaderless and Al alive in a cell? Raiders will be sloppier and angrier.
Big Al is taken alive. A cage is a poor end for anyone with a blade. The flatskins call it mercy.
They took Big Al and didn't kill them. In the Kingdom we would ask what the blade was for. The Stone Rats will squabble.
Big Al, caged. A living enemy is a debt unpaid. I hope the jailer keeps good count.
A prisoner in a flatskin cell. Let the jailer count the bars. The bars won't thank him. Raids may come in his name.
Big Al lives on in a cage. Okran gives even the lost a chance to repent, though few use it.
Chains for Big Al. If the chains are honest, the Flame is satisfied. The Stone Rats will squabble.
Big Al in chains. May the jailers be pure of heart, and unsentimental.
Big Al is taken alive. Let them repent in a cell. The Flame is patient, and so is the Nation. Raids may come in his name.
Big Al finds you before you find him. Pay at the road, not at the gate.
Rats don't ask. They take. Al taught them that.
Never look at Al's eyes for long. They want the same thing mine do, and it's blood.
Stone Rat Village is a nest.
He's mad as a gutted garru, Al. That's why nobody's finished him.
You killed Al. You killed Al!
Look at the hands on that one. Those did Al.
The boss is dead and you walk past me? I'll make it worth your while to regret it.
He was a madman, aye, but he was our madman. Come here.
You're the one who ended Big Al. Folk are quiet around you for good reasons.
Hear you cleared out the Stone Rats' boss. The roads are a little safer for it.
Someone put the rat down. I won't say who.
Al's dead? Then the raids slow down for a while.
Al's gone and the Village is open. You've done us a quiet kindness.
We'd planned on doing it ourselves. Thanks for saving us a funeral.
Big Al's gone and the rats are in the open. The village will turn to us soon enough.
A good day's work in the Stone Rat Village. We'll keep your name quiet.
Grim, finished? Hah! Now who does the Hounds' dirty work? Me, probably.
You got her? Good. Then you know I'm next.
Grim, dead? Then who will pay my rats? Hah! Not me, that's for sure.
You came to the rats' nest after killing Grim. Either very brave or very dim.
Darkbrow's dead, and I'd bet my knife one of our own had a hand in it. He never trusted a soul.
He sold his friends before he bought them lunch. And somebody finally charged him interest.
Blackshifters will carry on. We always do. We carry on in the dark and we don't ask where it goes.
Eh. The Hounds won't take Shark through us. Not without paying for the doorway.
Who's the new brow, then? Who has the eyes for it? Sit down, shut up, we're counting hands.
Darkbrow's gone. I'll say it plain: nothing changes. Shark's still Shark.
That traitor finally ran out of people to sell. The Blackshifters are stunned.
Big Darkbrow dead, Grim and Gray still breathing. A small day. Don't let it grow.
Hear Darkbrow's people are fighting over his hideout. Let them. Idiots eat each other.
Some swamp gangster named Dark-something got killed.
The Blackshifters lost their boss. Didn't think they had one.
Trouble in the swamp again. I stopped listening at the third body.
Somebody killed a swamp boss named Darkbrow. I hear he sold out his own kin. Fine.
They say Darkbrow fell to an outsider. The Kingdom respects a fair challenge, whoever answers it.
Darkbrow is dead and the Stone Golem didn't stir. It doesn't stir for such as that. The Blackshifters will quarrel over it.
So Darkbrow is gone. Let the flatskins fight over what is left.
Darkbrow fell, they say. A warrior who falls in the open has had a better end than most flatskins earn. Nobody grieves in the swamp.
I heard Darkbrow fell. I don't ask by whose hand. The Nation doesn't need the names of the righteous.
So Darkbrow is dead. Another sin put out. The Flame burns clean, and the ash is sensible about it. The Blackshifters will quarrel over it.
Darkbrow is gone. Say a prayer for the soul, if it had one. Then keep walking.
No tears from me for Darkbrow. Okran's mercy has limits, and the road marks them. Nobody grieves in the swamp.
Darkbrow, caged. Funny. He always said he'd be the one holding the key.
Somebody took him alive, and he's got a hundred secrets. Hope they stay shut.
If he talks, half of Shark is in trouble. If he doesn't, he's tougher than I thought.
Don't look so worried. He sold out his own mother twice. He'll sell out his jailer once.
Big Darkbrow in a cell. The man who sold his own friends, waiting for a friend.
Hounds smell blood. The Blackshifters are leaderless, and Shark is thin on shadows tonight.
Nobody will rescue Darkbrow out of love. Wait for the price.
Big Darkbrow caged. The Blackshifters just lost their sharpest knife.
He'll talk. It's what he does. The question is who he talks to.
Never turn your back on Darkbrow. Never turn your front, either.
The Blackshifters work at night. Every night. For whoever pays best, and then for the other fellow.
Darkbrow has a hideout in Shark and a knife in every pocket. Guess which one's meant for you.
He's loyal to the winning side. Watch which side that is, and ask who's winning.
You're the shadow that took Darkbrow. Shadows can be stepped on.
Blood for the boss. Not out of love, mind. Out of habit.
Everyone says you killed him. Funny. I only wanted his chair.
Darkbrow's dead and the Blackshifters answer to no one now.
That's the one who got Darkbrow. Keep your coin close and your sword closer.
Hear you ended that old traitor. Nobody here's crying about it.
So you're the one who finished Darkbrow. I never liked him either.
Hush. Everybody here knows what you did.
Grim, gone? Then the docks are mine. And you're welcome in my shadow.
You did it. You did it clean. Name your price. I don't pay it, but name it.
Grim, dead, and you at my door. We should talk about the sale of Shark.
You've done my work for me. You won't be paid for it.
Gray dead? Honest men break easy. I'm told it's a character flaw.
Grayflayers will be headless by dawn. I'll offer them a roof.
Gray dead. Hm. The Grayflayers will want a new roof.
He was honest. It was bound to kill him sooner or later.
Fang's gone. Cut down, I heard. Two blades and still it wasn't enough.
Nobody leads like Fang. Nobody dies like him either, I'll give him that.
Mud Town is quiet. The mud's still the mud. The bar's still the bar. But Fang's chair is cold.
Twinblades! Pick up your swords. I won't have the whole swamp saying we went soft.
Fang once cut a man in half to win an argument. Who finished an argument with him?
Big Fang finally got put down. Mud Town lost its loudest bully.
Grayflayers want Mud Town? Hounds want it? Twinblades don't have the stomach to say no.
Fang's the only boss with nothing to hold him up. No deal, no letter, no pact. Guess he stood alone.
A man who fights for the sake of fighting runs out of fights. He found his last one.
A swamp warlord named Fang was struck down. The swamp rejoices. Or doesn't.
Fang of the Twinblades is dead, someone said. Never heard of him, but I'm sure he deserved it.
Swamp gangs losing their heads one after another. I'd be nervous if I were in a Hound's boots.
Twinblades lost their leader, somebody said. Never heard of him.
People say Fang fell to an outsider. The Kingdom respects a fair challenge, whoever answers it.
Fang is dead and the Stone Golem did not stir. It does not stir for such as that. The Twinblades will quarrel over it.
So Fang is gone. Let the flatskins fight over what's left.
Fang fell, they say. A warrior who falls in the open has had a better end than most flatskins earn. Swamp blades change hands quickly.
I heard Fang fell. I do not ask by whose hand. The Nation does not need the names of the righteous.
So Fang is dead. Another sin put out. The Flame burns clean, and the ash is sensible about it. The Twinblades will quarrel over it.
Fang is gone. Say a prayer for the soul, if it had one. Then keep walking.
No tears from me for Fang. Okran's mercy has limits, and the road marks them. Swamp blades change hands quickly.
They shackled Fang. The man who couldn't be taken, taken. By one stranger, they say.
If he lives, he'll come back with two blades and a long memory.
He'll chew his chains. I'll bet you ten cats.
Fang, in chains. Something somewhere is about to break.
Fang is in a cage. First time that animal's been quiet in years.
Somebody took Big Fang alive. I'd have preferred they'd killed him.
Fang's locked up. The Twinblades are boiling. Stay out of Mud Town tonight.
I'd say it's a relief but I've seen a caged beast before. They don't stay caged.
Fang's got two blades and one rule: more blood than the other fellow.
Don't stare at Fang in Mud Town. He takes it as a request.
Twinblades don't take sides. They take everything.
Fang smiles before he kills. That's how you know to start running.
You killed Fang. Show me how, now. Show me, with me watching.
Two blades, one grudge. Come on, you!
Fang's blood is on your hands. I'll settle it with mine.
Fang's dead and I'm still sharpening mine. You'd better run.
You did Big Fang? Then you did me a favour I never asked for.
That's the stranger who cut down Fang. Seems small, for the job.
You killed Fang? Good. Everyone in Mud Town is trying not to dance.
That's the one who put Fang down. Don't buy them a drink. They might think you want something.
You took Grim, huh? You're brave and you smell it. Stand aside, we've got swamp to carve.
Hounds without Grim... Hah. Even better.
Grim, gone. And you come to me. Brave. Or stupid. Maybe both, same as me.
Good. Big dogs make for loud swamps. I like it quiet. I like it bloody and quiet.
Big Gray is dead. The only boss in the swamp who stole from the right people. And now this.
He kept his word, Gray. In a place like this, that's a death sentence.
The village will go to the Swampers. Our own people, ironically. They'll sell us for scrap.
Honour's cold comfort in the ground. I hope he got some before it went in.
The contracts will dry up, the heists will stop, and the Grayflayers will start eating each other.
I never thought anyone would put Gray down. He was so steady. A rock doesn't die.
Cut a clean mind out of the swamp and what grows in its place? Ask the Blood Spiders.
Swampers moving into our village! Shame on every one of us who let it happen.
We worked for the big payers and we stole from the bad. Who's left to tell which is which?
The Grayflayers lost their boss. Swampers will pick up the village.
Big Gray, dead. If Grim and Darkbrow follow him, Rot belongs to the Blood Spiders. I'd start praying.
Honest men in this swamp don't last. That's the lesson of Big Gray, I'd say.
He did the heist work no one else wanted. Now no one will do it.
A swamp gang called the Grayflayers lost their boss. Not that I knew they had one.
Big Gray? Oh, the careful thief. Dead. Shame, he never robbed me.
Rumour says Rot is ripe for the spiders. I'm not going near Rot.
The honest gangster of the swamp is dead. That's a sentence I never thought I'd say.
Big Gray is dead. A flatskin matter, but a death by the blade is the only kind worth hearing of.
Word is, Big Gray fell to an outsider. The Kingdom respects a fair challenge, whoever answers it. The Grayflayers are a swamp matter.
Big Gray is dead and the Stone Golem didn't stir. It doesn't stir for such as that.
So Big Gray is gone. Let the flatskins fight over what's left. They always do. Rot won't be quiet long.
Dead, Big Gray. May the unrepentant find the Flame waiting. May the rest of us find a quiet road.
I heard Big Gray fell. I don't ask by whose hand. The Nation doesn't need the names of the righteous. The Grayflayers are a swamp matter.
So Big Gray is dead. Another sin put out. The Flame burns clean, and the ash is sensible about it.
Big Gray is gone. Say a prayer for the soul, if it had one. Then keep walking. Rot won't be quiet long.
They've got Gray in chains. Never took him for a man to be taken.
Somebody took the honest one alive.
Gray won't break. But we will, if he stays gone.
Gray won't beg. If they've got him, they've got a hard bargain in front of them.
Gray's in chains, and the Swampers are circling the village already.
A boss who keeps his word, locked up. Swamp's going to miss that.
Gray in chains. Somebody will move in on Grayflayer Village, and soon.
Honest men don't last in a cage. Neither do the rest of us.
Big Gray steals from the bad and never from the poor. Ask anyone.
Gray pays his people on time. In the swamp that's practically a miracle.
Grayflayers have a code. Short, but they keep it.
Never owe Gray. Not because he'd hurt you. Because he'd forgive you, and that's worse.
You killed a man who never raised a hand to anyone who didn't deserve it. Come here.
Honour dies hard in the Grayflayers.
Gray's name is on your head now, stranger.
Gray was the last of us who kept to the rules. Come, fight like it matters.
You're the one that downed Gray. Honest man, honest mistake, I suppose.
That's the face that ended the Grayflayers' boss. Be careful in Shark.
You killed Gray? I don't know whether to shake your hand or burn it.
Gray's gone. Whatever's left of his village might as well be yours.
Grim dead? That's no good for any of us. A swamp without one strong hand is a swamp for spiders.
You've started something, stranger. I hope you can finish it.
Grim, dead? I hope you see what you've done. The Spiders can smell it from here.
A strong hand removed, stranger. Make sure someone else steps in.
The King is dead. Say it again. No, say it slower, I want to hear it properly.
Who collects the tolls now? Who decides who's a friend and who's a corpse?
I swore I'd die in that tower. Funny how it was him who did the dying.
Some outlander walked up the stairs and the whole kingdom came down. I was there for the noise.
Dust Bosses are already pulling knives over the crown. By nightfall we'll be forty kings.
He called every one of us friend. He called the outposts friends too, then took their food. Hah.
Take off the banners. Hide the stash. When a king falls, the first thing that goes is the order.
Best of friends, he used to say. Now I don't know who my friends are.
No more demands for cats on the road. Who'd have thought a bandit could be nostalgic?
Whoever killed him can come collect our tribute too. We've nobody left to give it to.
Half the Dust Bandits will drift north. The other half will starve. I'm betting on the second.
He smelled like old sweat and expensive oil and I loved him dearly.
There'll be a new king by the full moon, and he'll have to be worse. I'm told it's the only way.
The Dust King's dead. The roads out here just got a good deal safer. For a month, perhaps.
No more bandit demands at the outpost, so I hear. I'll believe it when a season passes without them.
Someone walked into that tower and killed the King. All of it. The guards and everything. I'd shake their hand if I wasn't afraid of the handshake.
He taxed every honest traveller in the dust. Now he's the one paying.
The Dust Bandits will break into squabbling pieces. Watch the roads for stray gangs with no one to answer to.
I raised a toast. Quietly. Dust bandits drink in the same bars.
They killed the Dust King, I hear. That big bounty on his head has been collected, one way or another.
The king of the dust bandits is dead. I'd say good riddance but I never had to cross his road.
Heard something about a tower falling and a king dying in it. Might be a tall story.
Whoever did it should be given a medal. Or a bounty, in case they do it again.
A famous bandit, that Dust King. Now he's famous for being dead.
The Dust King fell, they say. A warrior who falls in the open has had a better end than most flatskins earn.
Word came over the border. The Dust King is dead. We nodded, and went back to our cups. The dust road will change hands.
I didn't know the Dust King. I know the sort. The sort ends the way it ended.
A flatskin name has gone quiet. I heard it from a trader. I didn't ask for the rest. The bounty will be argued over.
No tears from me for the Dust King. Okran's mercy has limits, and the road marks them.
The Dust King is dead. The Flame doesn't weep for sinners. It does keep count. The dust road will change hands.
They say the Dust King is dead. Okran sees all, and has now seen the end of that one.
The Dust King has been struck down. Pray the deed was clean, and pray it wasn't ours to answer for. The bounty will be argued over.
They've got the King in chains. In chains! He used to say prison was for people who couldn't pay.
The tower's waiting. The throne's empty. Somebody go fetch him before the Dust Bosses get ideas.
He'll talk his way out. He's best of friends with everyone, remember.
A caged king is a joke. A joke that bites.
I keep pointing at his chair as if he'll be in it. Still empty.
The Dust King, locked up? I'd pay to see that. I'd pay more to see who guards him.
Bandit king captured alive. Somebody wants him to answer for something. Or somebody wants the bounty, which is the same.
Dust Bandits are headless. Expect raids by desperate men who don't know what they're doing.
Whoever caught him has either got nerves of iron or a death wish. Good for the roads either way.
Come out and talk to your friendly neighbours, the King says. We only want to be friends.
The Dust King's tower has never been taken. Nobody's tried since the last fellow, and look where he is.
Pay up and you're a friend of the King. Don't pay and you're a story we tell the new boys.
Hate the King all you like. He's the reason we eat.
I pay the Dust King's toll twice a year and he thanks me every time. Best of friends, he says.
Don't take the dust road unless you're carrying spare cats. The King collects.
Three nations want that man's head. He's still on it. Make of that what you will.
The Dust King sends lovely letters. Wrapped around a knife, of course.
The Dust King still stands. The flatskin lands have many such. The Kingdom keeps its own counsel.
